subject: Competitive match request — reconciliation of quote and SLA clarifications
messages:
From: Elaine Kim <elaine.kim@neptuneanalytics.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@neptuneanalytics.com
Date: Mon, 4 May 2026 16:03:00 -0700
Subject: Initial RFP + incumbent match request

Hi Mina —

Thanks for taking the time earlier. Attached is our updated RFP and the incumbent vendor’s final commercial that the procurement team has asked us to present for any match requests. Key items they care about: overall price parity on committed AI-hours, a 30-day onboarding plan with go-live milestones, and a tighter SLA (99.9% p95 for API latency).

High level: Neptune is evaluating a 12-month committed throughput purchase with a 3-month pilot. The incumbent has offered a blended effective rate that includes an onboarding credit (one-month equivalent) and an egress carveout.

Can Redwood provide a reconciliation of your standard quote vs an adjusted quote that lines up to their blended numbers? We need the commercial and a simple one-page note on how Redwood covers the egress and onboarding credits. Procurement wants to receive anything they can push to legal by EOD Wednesday.

Attachments: Neptune_RFP_v2.pdf (PDF), incumbent_final_commercial.xlsx (XLSX)

Best,
Elaine
Head of Procurement, Neptune Analytics

From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
To: Elaine Kim <elaine.kim@neptuneanalytics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 4 May 2026 19:14:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Initial RFP + incumbent match request

Hi Elaine —

Thanks for the RFP and the incumbent sheet — that helps. Quick clarifying questions so we reconcile apples-to-apples:

- Can you confirm the committed metric the incumbent used (token-hours vs endpoint-hours vs seat licensing)?
- Is the onboarding credit applied as a $ credit on the first invoice or as waived usage?
- Any mandatory data residency/egress carveouts we should reflect?

Short answer: we can match effective economics on committed throughput with two levers — a) a one-time onboarding credit (we typically offer 25–50% of month-1 committed spend for 3-month pilots) and b) an egress carveout that can be limited by region and retention window. We’ll need to align on the exact usage profile to size the credit.

I’m attaching a working draft of a reconciled quote and a proposed SLA addendum for your legal team to triage. If procurement needs a simple redline, let me know and Marissa can push directly to them.

Next steps I propose:
- You confirm the incumbent’s committed metric + sample monthly run-rate (by May 5 COB)
- Redwood will return a reconciled quote and a 1-page explanation of the math (by May 6 morning)
- If accepted, we’ll generate a DocuSign with an SLA addendum and onboarding milestones for signature.

Attachments: Redline_Reconciled_Quote_draft.pdf (PDF), SLA-Addendum-draft.docx (DOCX)

Thanks,
Mina Haddad
Head of Commercial — Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 4 May 2026 20:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: RE: Initial RFP + incumbent match request

Mina / Marissa —

Quick internal notes on margin and legal risk before we finalize the recon:

- If we replicate the incumbent blended rate exactly, margin impact on the first 3 months is ~18% assuming their reported egress carveout of 1.2TB/mo. If Neptune’s usage is heavier on embeddings/caching, the unit economics shift further. Suggest we tie the on-ramp credit to a pilot volume threshold to protect against heavy tail usage.
- Legal will push back on an open-ended egress carveout. Recommend we propose region-limited carveouts (US-only) and a 90-day retention cap.
- SLA: 99.9% p95 is ok but only with a rollback clause if their run-rate spikes beyond committed throughput. We should include a reconciliation cadence (monthly) in the SLA.

I’ll draft the pricing note for the reconciled PDF and flag the protective terms in the SLA addendum. Marissa — can you run updated numbers for a 12-month commit with a 3-month pilot and an onboarding credit equal to 30% of month-1? Need by tomorrow AM.

-Jonas

From: Elaine Kim <elaine.kim@neptuneanalytics.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@neptuneanalytics.com
Date: Tue, 5 May 2026 09:42:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Initial RFP + incumbent match request

Thanks Mina and team — answers below.

- Incumbent committed metric: "API compute hours" with a blended effective rate after credits. We have sample month usage in the RFP (see Table B).
- Onboarding credit: they applied a one-month credit against invoice 1 (so invoiced amount month 1 = 0 for committed portion).
- Egress: incumbent excluded egress charges for EU and US under 2TB/month; anything above that is billed.

Procurement timeline: procurement needs a commercial (quote + one-paragraph legal note) to circulate by EOD Wednesday. If you can provide a DocuSign-ready contract, procurement can start signatures on May 10.

We can be flexible on carveouts by region, but please call out any hard limits in the commercial. Also, add a short onboarding milestone table that shows the 30/60/90 day checkpoints.

Attachments: procurement_form.pdf (PDF)

Elaine

From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
To: Elaine Kim <elaine.kim@neptuneanalytics.com>, procurement@neptuneanalytics.com
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 5 May 2026 18:22:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Initial RFP + incumbent match request — Consolidated quote and next steps

Elaine / procurement team —

Attached is a consolidated quote (Redwood-Consolidated-Quote-NP-2026-023.pdf) that reconciles to the incumbent’s blended numbers under these assumptions: committed metric = API compute hours; onboarding credit = one-month equivalent applied as invoice credit; egress carveout = US + EU under 2TB/month; pilot volume cap = first 90 days up to 1.5x reported run-rate to avoid tail risk.

Key callouts (one-paragraph legal note included inside the PDF):
- Onboarding credit: one-time invoice credit equal to 100% of committed month 1 for the committed portion (we can reduce to 50% if Neptune prefers to spread over two invoices).
- Egress carveout: US/EU up to 2TB/month; overage billed at standard egress rates.
- SLA: we accept 99.9% p95 for the committed endpoints with a monthly reconciliation clause and a pre-defined rollback threshold if usage in a single month exceeds 180% of committed throughput.

Next steps:
1) Procurement confirms they received the quote and legal note (please confirm by EOD Wednesday).
2) I’ll generate a DocuSign packet (contract + SLA addendum) for signature targeting May 10.
3) Onboarding PM will be copied once contract is signed; 30/60/90 day milestone table in the attachment.

Attachments: Redwood-Consolidated-Quote-NP-2026-023.pdf (PDF), SLA-Addendum-draft.docx (DOCX)

Thanks,
Mina
Head of Commercial — Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
